text:
Minnesota arrives on the second night of a back-to-back after a 5-1 win at SEA last night, and it's 3-1-1 in its last five, without Marcus Foligno and Nick Foligno. Vancouver hasn't won in nine (0-8-1) and has been outscored 41-18 in that stretch, with the chances (35% of the expected goals) backing up the results. Add Quinn Hughes, who makes his first trip back to Vancouver after 459 games with the Canucks and sits one point shy of 500 career points, and the night has some weight.

The numbers favor MIN. At five on five, the Wild have taken 55% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) in their games, VAN 40%, and our model has MIN scoring 3.67 to VAN's 2.65. The special-teams matchup to watch is MIN's power play, which generates 0.88 expected goals a game against a VAN penalty kill allowing 0.98. In net, Calvin Pickard is the projected starter for MIN over Jesper Wallstedt, who has 11 of 12 starts. Pickard sits at -2.2 goals saved above expected (how many goals a goalie stops compared with an average one facing the same shots) this season. Leevi Meriläinen, projected for VAN, is at +2.3 this season but -17.9 last year.

Kirill Kaprizov is 54% to score and 81% for a point, and Matt Boldy is 47% to score. Hughes is 76% for a point. Our under-the-radar pick is Joel Eriksson Ek, 61% for a point, his line creating 4.94 expected goals per 60 against a VAN defense that gives up the second-most. Minnesota's rest disadvantage and the Pickard start are in our numbers, so they matter.
